Impossible de parler de l'entrepreneuria: It's impossible to talk about entrepreneurship in Montréal without thinking of Alexandre Kénol. Manager of the Tiers Lieu, arts promoter and coach.
Pour avoir grandi entre Laval et Montréa: Having grown up between Laval and Montréal-Nord, the young entrepreneur of Haitian origin shares how he juggled two neighbourhoods to get the best out of both and build himself into an inspiring citizen. He welcomes us at the Tiers Lieu, a co-working space he founded in Laval to meet the entrepreneurial needs of the city and the North Shore.
Alex est un homme occupé. Très occupé. «: Alex is a busy man. A very busy man. “I wear a lot of hats,” he begins, laughing. “When people ask me what I do these days, I always answer by saying what I don't do. It's simpler.”
Alex a une posture imposante. L’énergie: Alex has an imposing presence. At six feet tall, though, the energy he gives off is warm. “Welcome to my place,” he says between bursts of laughter as he greets us at his company's offices.
Au Tiers Lieu, l'homme de 35 ans prône u: At the Tiers Lieu, the 35-year-old champions a caring, community-minded corporate workspace. “Here, we're convinced that economic, social and cultural success comes through getting involved in the community and through collaboration between people from different backgrounds,” he explains.
En plus de son rôle de directeur général: In addition to his role as general manager of the Tiers Lieu, in 2019 he founded Geak a company that organizes community engagement events for businesses.
Il crée aussi la plateforme d’artistes <: He also created the artist platform Feaster, which he runs on the side. Through this platform, Alex promotes local talent that, he believes, doesn't get enough exposure.
Grand passionné de sport, il entraîne au: A big sports fan, he also coaches the women's soccer team at Collège Montmorency in Laval. For him, “sport is what brings communities together,” he says, pushing his round glasses up his nose. It only makes sense that he devotes part of his time to it.
Jeune lavallois, il a grandi entre son q: A young Laval native, he grew up between his home neighbourhood, Vimont, and Montréal-Nord, where his grandmother lived. “I spent a lot of time with her back then. I was very close to her,” he says. For Alex, growing up with one foot on each side of the river was a good thing: “I was lucky to grow up in Montréal-Nord, because I made a ton of friends there,” he recalls.
Alex a grandi dans une famille «typiquem: Alex grew up in a “typical Haitian family from Montréal,” he tells us. He remembers his teenage years, when his parents had high academic expectations of him, and it wasn't always easy for the entrepreneur to break through those traditional barriers. “Me, I'm a project guy. When I talked to my father about the entrepreneurial ideas I had in mind, he didn't want to hear anything about it,” he recalls.
Il se rappelle même d’une conversation a: He even remembers one conversation with his father: “If you're not aiming for a job as a doctor, lawyer, architect or accountant, it's like you're not speaking French to me: I won't understand what you're telling me,” his father said at the time, a memory Alex now recounts with a touch of humour in his voice.
S’il en rigole aujourd’hui, ça n’a pas t: He laughs about it today, but it wasn't always that way. “It was complicated to stand out from the crowd and to be seen as a misfit by your parents,” he admits. He stares into the distance, seemingly lost in his past, and adds that this period wasn't hard only for his family, but for everyone around him.
Que ce soit à Laval ou à Montréal, il sa: Whether in Laval or in Montréal, he knew he was “a little different” from the others. “I always wanted to push the door open, to go further. I did that because I saw the violent reality facing kids in the neighbourhood, and I wanted to give myself more options,” he explains.
La lumière à travers la grande baie vitr: The light through the large bay window of the Tiers Lieu begins to fade little by little, signalling the start of sunset. It's the moment Alex chooses to tell us what he did so as not to “sink into the bad circumstances of the street, like violence or crime.”
En effet, il n’a pas toujours été possib: Indeed, it wasn't always possible for him to ignore the problems tied to the street. “I looked at other paths that turned out to be easier. I was incredibly lucky to be well surrounded, because I quickly understood that ‘easy’ money wasn't really easy,” he reveals. He also feels eternal gratitude toward his parents: “even though they weren't necessarily thrilled at the idea of me doing something other than what they had planned for me, they helped me enormously to stay on the straight and narrow.”
Questionné sur les opportunités qu’il a: Asked about the opportunities he came across in his journey, the soccer coach answers without missing a beat: “the first doors that opened for me, I had to bust them down.”
En grandissant, il voit en effet que cer: As he grew up, he saw that some people managed to reach their goals. He didn't understand why he couldn't do it as easily. Yet he had ambition and did everything it took to succeed: he enrolled in university in management, gained leadership experience by creating the Laval futsal league, and threw himself body and soul into entrepreneurship. Then reality caught up with him: “when you're a Black man and you have projects, you have two, even three times as many obstacles to clear. That's the main reason I try to get as involved as I can with my community, whether through my work or through my determination,” he says, his eyes bright.

S’il a eu à travailler si fort pour en a: Having had to work so hard to get where he is today, putting in long hours and throwing himself into every role he has held over time, he doesn't want the next generation to go through the same thing. “I try to give back by always being available for young people. I'm a coach today, but I also like going into schools to give talks and tell kids how to succeed in entrepreneurship, especially when you come from a racialized community,” he explains.
Extrêmement reconnaissant lorsqu’il s’im: Extremely grateful whenever he gets involved with young people, Alex feels that he is the lucky one to be around them, not the other way around.
«Il y a des jeunes qui vivent certaines: “There are young people going through certain things who may never be able to talk about them. What they don't know is that there are other people who have been through the same murky places,” he explains. “Having a big-brother or big-sister outlook toward them can play a huge role in their motivation and help them.”
Que ça soit par l’intermédiaire de son r: Whether through his role as a coach or as a mentor, Alex always comes back to the same refrain. According to him, we have to build on the uniqueness of each young person and break down the negative view each one may have of themselves. “Everyone's abilities are different. The point I make, and will always keep defending, is to never compare yourself,” he says in a message meant for anyone willing to hear it.
Avant que l’on ne quitte le Tiers Lieu,: Before we leave the Tiers Lieu, Alex makes one last confession. One of the most important lessons he has learned: “nothing truly worthwhile comes without a steep price.” What he encourages is ambition and determination. “You have to go for it,” he concludes, cheerful.
